**Fill in each blank (1)–(4) with the correct word from the box below. There are more words than you need — some words will not be used.**

**Word box:** together — wasting — spices — selling — returning — carrying

Every Saturday morning, Ama goes to the market with her grandmother. Today is a special day because Ama's brother is (1)_____ from Yaounde after two years abroad. Grandmother wants to prepare a big meal, so she asks the seller for the fattest chicken in his basket. Ama helps by (2)_____ the vegetables into a large basket while her grandmother pays for the meat. On their way home, they stop at a small shop to buy a bag of rice and some (3)_____ for the sauce. Ama is excited because, for the first time in two years, the whole family will be (4)_____ around the same table.
corrige_markdown:
### Rappel de méthode
Dans un texte à trous continu, il faut d'abord lire l'ensemble du passage sans s'arrêter aux blancs, pour saisir l'histoire globale. Ensuite, pour chaque blanc, on identifie la nature du mot attendu (verbe, nom, adjectif) et le sens exigé par le contexte proche ET par les informations données ailleurs dans le texte, avant de choisir dans la banque de mots.

### Corrigé
Every Saturday morning, Ama goes to the market with her grandmother. Today is a special day because Ama's brother is **returning** from Yaounde after two years abroad. Grandmother wants to prepare a big meal, so she asks the seller for the fattest chicken in his basket. Ama helps by **carrying** the vegetables into a large basket while her grandmother pays for the meat. On their way home, they stop at a small shop to buy a bag of rice and some **spices** for the sauce. Ama is excited because, for the first time in two years, the whole family will be **together** around the same table.

**Justification blanc par blanc :**
1. **returning** — seul mot du bloc qui complète logiquement « is ___ from Yaounde after two years abroad » ; « selling »/« wasting » ne conviennent pas grammaticalement dans cette tournure.
2. **carrying** — complète « helps by ___ the vegetables into a basket » ; « selling » contredirait le sens (on ne vend pas ses propres légumes en les mettant dans un panier).
3. **spices** — seul nom d'ingrédient de la banque adapté à « some ___ for the sauce ».
4. **together** — se déduit de l'information donnée en début de texte (« two years abroad ») reprise en fin de texte (« for the first time in two years ») : la famille sera réunie.

**Mots-pièges non utilisés :** wasting (ne s'accorde avec aucun blanc), selling (grammaticalement tentant au blanc 2 mais contredit le sens de la phrase).

**Fill in each blank (1)–(5) with the correct word from the box below. There are more words than you need — some words will not be used.**

**Word box:** quickly — friend — earlier — homework — share — good — play

Fabrice was very nervous on his first day at his new school in Douala. He did not know anyone in his class, and he sat alone near the window. During break time, a boy named Junior came and sat next to him. Junior asked Fabrice if he wanted to (1)_____ his sandwich, and Fabrice said yes with a shy smile. The two boys quickly discovered that they both (2)_____ football on Wednesday afternoons. By the end of the day, Fabrice was no longer afraid, because he had already made a new (3)_____. When he got home, he told his mother that his first day had finally become a (4)_____ one. The next morning, he woke up (5)_____ than usual because he could not wait to see Junior again.
corrige_markdown:
### Rappel de méthode
Pour un texte à trous narratif, chaque blanc doit être résolu à partir de la logique de l'histoire entière, pas seulement de la phrase où il se trouve : un sentiment mentionné au début peut être confirmé ou transformé plus loin dans le texte. Élimine d'abord les mots de la banque dont la nature grammaticale ne correspond pas à l'espace à remplir.

### Corrigé
Fabrice was very nervous on his first day at his new school in Douala. He did not know anyone in his class, and he sat alone near the window. During break time, a boy named Junior came and sat next to him. Junior asked Fabrice if he wanted to **share** his sandwich, and Fabrice said yes with a shy smile. The two boys quickly discovered that they both **play** football on Wednesday afternoons. By the end of the day, Fabrice was no longer afraid, because he had already made a new **friend**. When he got home, he told his mother that his first day had finally become a **good** one. The next morning, he woke up **earlier** than usual because he could not wait to see Junior again.

**Justification blanc par blanc :**
1. **share** — seul verbe de la banque qui convient après « wanted to ___ his sandwich » ; « homework » est un nom, « quickly » un adverbe, aucun ne peut occuper cette place de verbe.
2. **play** — s'accorde avec « they both ___ football », sujet pluriel + base verbale.
3. **friend** — complète « made a new ___ », nom attendu après « new ».
4. **good** — se déduit de l'ensemble de l'histoire (peur au début, amitié trouvée à la fin) : la journée est devenue positive.
5. **earlier** — comparatif attendu après « woke up ___ than usual » ; « quickly » ne peut pas former de comparatif sous cette forme (« quickly than » est incorrect).

**Mots-pièges non utilisés :** homework (mauvaise nature grammaticale pour tous les blancs), quickly (ne peut pas s'utiliser en comparatif avec « than » sous cette forme).

**Fill in each blank (1)–(5) with the correct word from the box below. There are more words than you need — some words will not be used.**

**Word box:** seasoned — chair — first — dropped — second — confidence — forget

Rosine had practised her cassava-and-groundnut recipe every evening for two weeks before the Home Economics contest. On the morning of the contest, she woke up early and packed her ingredients into a basket, making sure not to (1)_____ the small bag of spices her grandmother had given her. When it was her turn to cook in front of the judges, her hands began to shake, and she almost (2)_____ the pot of boiling water. Remembering her grandmother's advice to stay calm and taste the sauce often, Rosine took a deep breath and continued stirring with more (3)_____. Ten minutes later, the head judge tasted her dish and smiled, telling the other judges that the sauce was perfectly (4)_____. Rosine could hardly believe that the recipe she had feared forgetting was now the reason she had just won the (5)_____ prize of the entire competition, beating twelve other students.
corrige_markdown:
### Rappel de méthode
Un texte à trous cohérent construit souvent un fil narratif où la fin du texte confirme un choix fait plus tôt. Avant de répondre, repère les indices disséminés dans tout le passage (une inquiétude annoncée au début, un résultat donné à la fin) et vérifie que ton choix pour chaque blanc reste cohérent avec l'ensemble de l'histoire, pas seulement avec la phrase immédiate.

### Corrigé
Rosine had practised her cassava-and-groundnut recipe every evening for two weeks before the Home Economics contest. On the morning of the contest, she woke up early and packed her ingredients into a basket, making sure not to **forget** the small bag of spices her grandmother had given her. When it was her turn to cook in front of the judges, her hands began to shake, and she almost **dropped** the pot of boiling water. Remembering her grandmother's advice to stay calm and taste the sauce often, Rosine took a deep breath and continued stirring with more **confidence**. Ten minutes later, the head judge tasted her dish and smiled, telling the other judges that the sauce was perfectly **seasoned**. Rosine could hardly believe that the recipe she had feared forgetting was now the reason she had just won the **first** prize of the entire competition, beating twelve other students.

**Justification blanc par blanc :**
1. **forget** — confirmé plus loin dans le texte par « the recipe she had feared forgetting », qui reprend exactement cette idée.
2. **dropped** — seul verbe de la banque cohérent avec « her hands began to shake, and she almost ___ the pot ».
3. **confidence** — nom attendu après « with more ___ », en cohérence avec le conseil de rester calme.
4. **seasoned** — adjectif qui décrit positivement une sauce réussie, confirmé par le sourire du juge.
5. **first** — déduit de « beating twelve other students » : si elle bat tous les autres, elle ne peut être que première, pas deuxième.

**Mots-pièges non utilisés :** second (contredit « beating twelve other students »), chair (ne s'accorde avec aucun blanc, ni comme verbe ni comme nom dans ce contexte).

**Fill in each blank (1)–(5) with the correct word from the box below. There are more words than you need — some words will not be used.**

**Word box:** aisle — canceled — cover — purse — delayed — carry — release

Last Saturday, Serge and his family left their house very early to attend his cousin's wedding in Bafoussam, which was almost three hours away by bus. Everything went smoothly until the bus suddenly stopped in the middle of the road because the engine had begun to (1)_____ smoke. The driver stepped out, opened the bonnet, and told the passengers that the journey would be (2)_____ for at least an hour while he tried to fix the problem. Serge's mother started to worry because the wedding ceremony was due to begin at noon, and they still had ninety kilometres to (3)_____. Fortunately, a truck driver who was passing by noticed the stranded bus and offered to (4)_____ some of the passengers to the next town in his truck, where they could find another bus. Thanks to his kindness, Serge and his family arrived at the church just as the bride was walking down the (5)_____, and they quietly took their seats at the back.
corrige_markdown:
### Rappel de méthode
Dans un texte narratif à trous, certains mots de la banque peuvent sembler grammaticalement possibles mais être incompatibles avec un détail donné ailleurs dans le texte (une durée, un lieu, un événement annoncé au début). Confirme toujours ton choix en relisant tout le passage, pas seulement la phrase du blanc.

### Corrigé
Last Saturday, Serge and his family left their house very early to attend his cousin's wedding in Bafoussam, which was almost three hours away by bus. Everything went smoothly until the bus suddenly stopped in the middle of the road because the engine had begun to **release** smoke. The driver stepped out, opened the bonnet, and told the passengers that the journey would be **delayed** for at least an hour while he tried to fix the problem. Serge's mother started to worry because the wedding ceremony was due to begin at noon, and they still had ninety kilometres to **cover**. Fortunately, a truck driver who was passing by noticed the stranded bus and offered to **carry** some of the passengers to the next town in his truck, where they could find another bus. Thanks to his kindness, Serge and his family arrived at the church just as the bride was walking down the **aisle**, and they quietly took their seats at the back.

**Justification blanc par blanc :**
1. **release** — complète « the engine had begun to ___ smoke » ; ni « cover » ni « carry » ne s'associent naturellement à « smoke ».
2. **delayed** — confirmé par la suite de la même phrase (« while he tried to fix the problem ») : le voyage continue, il n'est donc pas annulé.
3. **cover** — collocation attendue avec une distance : « kilometres to cover ».
4. **carry** — précisé par « in his truck », ce qui élimine « cover » au sens de « payer/couvrir des frais ».
5. **aisle** — se déduit du mot « wedding » donné dès la première phrase du texte : la mariée avance dans l'allée de l'église.

**Mots-pièges non utilisés :** canceled (incompatible avec une durée précise, « for at least an hour »), purse (ne convient à aucun blanc).

**Fill in each blank (1)–(5) with the correct word from the box below. There are more words than you need — some words will not be used.**

**Word box:** merit — borrow — apply — time — bicycle — classroom — pay

When Nadège first suggested starting a recycling club at her school, most of her classmates thought the idea was a waste of (1)_____. They could not understand why anyone would want to collect used plastic bottles instead of playing football after lessons. Nadège did not give up; she explained that a company in town was ready to (2)_____ money for every kilogram of plastic the school collected, and that the money could buy new books for the library. Slowly, more students joined her, and within two months, the club had gathered enough bottles to fill an entire (3)_____. When the principal saw the enormous pile during the morning assembly, he announced that Nadège's club would receive a special certificate of (4)_____ at the end-of-year ceremony. The classmates who had once laughed at her idea were now the first to (5)_____ for a place on the club's committee.
corrige_markdown:
### Rappel de méthode
Pour ce type de texte, il faut souvent attendre la fin de l'histoire pour confirmer le sens exact d'un blanc situé plus tôt : un retournement de situation (le scepticisme initial qui se transforme en admiration) éclaire rétroactivement le choix du bon mot. Élimine aussi les mots dont la nature grammaticale ne correspond pas à l'espace à remplir.

### Corrigé
When Nadège first suggested starting a recycling club at her school, most of her classmates thought the idea was a waste of **time**. They could not understand why anyone would want to collect used plastic bottles instead of playing football after lessons. Nadège did not give up; she explained that a company in town was ready to **pay** money for every kilogram of plastic the school collected, and that the money could buy new books for the library. Slowly, more students joined her, and within two months, the club had gathered enough bottles to fill an entire **classroom**. When the principal saw the enormous pile during the morning assembly, he announced that Nadège's club would receive a special certificate of **merit** at the end-of-year ceremony. The classmates who had once laughed at her idea were now the first to **apply** for a place on the club's committee.

**Justification blanc par blanc :**
1. **time** — complète l'expression figée « a waste of ___ ».
2. **pay** — seul verbe de la banque cohérent avec « ready to ___ money for every kilogram ».
3. **classroom** — nom attendu après « fill an entire ___ », cohérent avec une grande quantité de bouteilles.
4. **merit** — complète l'expression « a certificate of ___ », confirmée par l'annonce officielle du principal.
5. **apply** — se déduit du retournement de situation raconté dans tout le texte : les élèves moqueurs veulent maintenant rejoindre le club.

**Mots-pièges non utilisés :** borrow (contredit la logique : une entreprise paie pour du plastique recyclé, elle ne l'emprunte pas), bicycle (ne s'accorde avec aucun blanc).

**Fill in each blank (1)–(5) with the correct word from the box below. There are more words than you need — some words will not be used.**

**Word box:** handed — silver — keep — ashamed — arrived — filled — money

As the bus pulled away from the station, Blaise noticed a brown wallet lying under the seat in front of him. He picked it up and quickly checked inside; it was (1)_____ with banknotes and an identity card showing a woman's photograph. For a moment, Blaise thought about keeping the money for himself, since nobody on the bus had seen him find it. However, he remembered how his father had once returned a lost goat to its rightful owner without expecting any reward, and the memory made him feel (2)_____ about his first idea. When the bus reached the next stop, Blaise noticed the same woman from the photograph standing anxiously by the door, searching through her bag. He walked over and (3)_____ her the wallet, explaining exactly where he had found it. The woman's face changed from worry to relief, and she thanked him with tears in her eyes, insisting that he (4)_____ some of the money as a reward. Blaise politely refused, saying that his father's lesson was worth far more than any (5)_____ he could have kept.
corrige_markdown:
### Rappel de méthode
Dans un texte à trous plus long, certains blancs ne peuvent se résoudre qu'en reliant une information donnée loin dans le texte (un détail mentionné au début, une valeur morale évoquée dans une phrase précédente) à la phrase du blanc lui-même. Ne te fie jamais à un mot qui « sonne bien » isolément : vérifie qu'il reste cohérent avec l'histoire entière avant de le retenir.

### Corrigé
As the bus pulled away from the station, Blaise noticed a brown wallet lying under the seat in front of him. He picked it up and quickly checked inside; it was **filled** with banknotes and an identity card showing a woman's photograph. For a moment, Blaise thought about keeping the money for himself, since nobody on the bus had seen him find it. However, he remembered how his father had once returned a lost goat to its rightful owner without expecting any reward, and the memory made him feel **ashamed** about his first idea. When the bus reached the next stop, Blaise noticed the same woman from the photograph standing anxiously by the door, searching through her bag. He walked over and **handed** her the wallet, explaining exactly where he had found it. The woman's face changed from worry to relief, and she thanked him with tears in her eyes, insisting that he **keep** some of the money as a reward. Blaise politely refused, saying that his father's lesson was worth far more than any **money** he could have kept.

**Justification blanc par blanc :**
1. **filled** — décrit le contenu du portefeuille (« with banknotes and an identity card ») ; « silver » ne convient pas au sens de la phrase, « arrived » est un verbe intransitif inadapté ici.
2. **ashamed** — se déduit de la phrase précédente (l'histoire du père qui rend une chèvre perdue) : ce souvenir moral fait honte à Blaise pour sa première idée.
3. **handed** — s'accorde avec le temps et la construction de la phrase (« walked over and ___ her the wallet ») ; « arrived » est intransitif et ne peut pas prendre de complément d'objet ici.
4. **keep** — forme verbale de base attendue après « insisting that he ___ », cohérente avec l'idée d'un cadeau qu'on garde.
5. **money** — reprend, en fin de texte, l'information donnée au tout début du récit (« filled with banknotes ») : ce que Blaise refuse est bien la somme trouvée dans le portefeuille.

**Mots-pièges non utilisés :** silver (ne s'accorde avec le sens d'aucun blanc), arrived (verbe intransitif, incompatible avec les constructions des blancs 1, 3 et 4).
